object_description: two similar separate buildings, each a large head with a lower annex, forming a courtyard between them
geometry_property: large head buildings with lower annexes
design_condition: two similar buildings with their annexes are grouped so they relate to each other and to the surrounding urban spaces, forming a permeable tree-lined courtyard that continues the city paths

positive: The volume fits well into the overall granularity of the district
Two head buildings with lower annexes relate easily to each other and to the surrounding urban spaces
A kind of quarter is created that appears composed of similar buildings and forms a courtyard inside
The courtyard is a spacious, permeable, tree-lined, attractive public space
The interplay of space widening and narrowing generates an interesting image for users moving through
The courtyard is part of a sequence of squares as well as a transitory space
It offers passage through the area without leading through the house
The design reacts sensitively to the surrounding urban space and incorporates traditional elements
The more intimate tree garden in the north forms a counterpoint
The tree selection refers to the location and gardens, forming a harmonious transition
A building system is created that takes up the city paths and continues them
This creates a very natural connection to the city, reflected in the building heights
The ensemble shows a plausible possibility of how the district could develop further
The university is seen as part of the city into which it is integrated
The distribution of usage between the two buildings seems plausible
The different heights are cleverly integrated into the sequence of open spaces
One always enters the buildings from the street, keeping them connected to the urban space in scale
The central courtyard in each head is well proportioned and offers good communication opportunities
The hybrid concrete and timber construction shows good environmental and sustainability values
It will develop a characteristic and appropriate atmosphere inside
The project has very good prerequisites for sustainability certification
A precise urban work strongly drawn to the small-scale development of the surrounding spaces
negative: Whether the courtyard also functions as a passageway remains to be discussed
The division into two buildings is difficult for the functional processes of the university
Flexibility of use requires some compromises
The duplication of courtyards prevents a central interior space for the university
The design language is mineral and solid, so the tin fluting seems a bit strange
Roof areas heavily occupied by photovoltaics conflict with the extensive green roofs
In space consumption and cost-effectiveness the project is in the last third
Not all requirements of the university can be met
